meta.title: Count the Stops
meta.textType: story: two children count ferry stops

paragraphs: On Saturday, January ninth, the Explorers went by boat to Hill Pier. They played in the river park and ate an early lunch. Then they took the boat back at quarter to twelve. The boat was crowded. Teacher Kim, Mia, and Lily found seats at the front. Leo and May sat down on a bench in the corner at the back. A woman with three big bags sat beside them. Her luggage took a lot of room, but she seemed kind. The back was far from Teacher Kim, so Leo and May could not see her. A voice said, "Next stop: Park Pier." "Is the next stop ours?" asked Leo. "I think so," he said. "I don't agree," said May. "We get off at Market Pier, and that is two stops after Hill Pier." Leo pointed at the diagram on the wall.

Leo looked at the diagram again. "Let's count the stops," said May. She held up two fingers. "Hill Pier, Park Pier, Market Pier," she counted. "Market Pier is the middle dot, and it is two stops after Hill Pier." "You are right," said Leo. "We are lucky that you can count." Soon the boat stopped at Park Pier. Then it came to a small pier with a sign: "MARKET PIER." "Excuse me," said May to the woman. The woman moved her bags, and the two friends stood at the open side of the boat. "Hurry, or the boat will leave!" said Leo. It was ten past twelve when they stepped onto the pier.

A fruit stall with a green awning stood near the end of the pier. Teacher Kim, Mia, and Lily were there, and they waved. Teacher Kim held a clipboard. A crate of oranges stood beside the stall. "Where were you?" asked Mia. "We counted the stops," said Leo. "Please stay here," said Teacher Kim. "We will go to the market at half past twelve."

"I was afraid that you were lost," said Lily. "We were not lost," said May. "I know that Market Pier is the middle stop." "I am sure that we got off at the right place." "I thought that the next stop was ours," said Leo. "May was right, and I was wrong." "I hope that you will count again next time," said Teacher Kim, and she smiled.
The seller cut an orange into pieces for the Explorers. Far away, the boat left the pier with the woman and her three big bags. Leo gave May the biggest piece, because she counted the stops.
text.summary: Leo and May sit at the back of a crowded ferry and cannot see Teacher Kim. When the voice says the next stop, they disagree about it, so they count the stops on the diagram and get off at the right pier.
